subsystems.name: Optical stack
subsystems.role: lets the mirror be a mirror and a screen at once.
parts: high-brightness LCD or OLED panel behind it

subsystems.name: Compute module
subsystems.role: runs vision, speech and assistant models locally where possible.

subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: gathers what the user is doing and saying.

subsystems.name: Vision and personalisation software
subsystems.role: recognises who is present and builds a profile of their preferences.

subsystems.name: Home automation bridge
subsystems.role: connects the mirror to lights, heating and other devices.

subsystems.name: Frame and enclosure
subsystems.role: mounts the unit on a wall and keeps electronics cool and dry.

buildSteps.title: Choose the optical arrangement
buildSteps.detail: A display sits behind half-silvered glass; brightness must be high enough that the screen shows through while the mirror still reflects in a lit room.

buildSteps.title: Design the enclosure
buildSteps.detail: The frame holds glass, panel, camera and microphones with a recessed camera angle and enough airflow to dissipate heat from a sealed box.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the display layer
buildSteps.detail: The panel is bonded to the glass with an optically clear layer so reflections and hotspots do not ruin the image.

buildSteps.title: Fit sensing hardware
buildSteps.detail: Camera and microphone array are positioned to see a person standing in front of the mirror and hear them from a few metres away.

buildSteps.title: Build the software stack
buildSteps.detail: On-device models handle wake word, face detection and speech recognition; only what is needed is sent to a larger model in the cloud.

buildSteps.title: Enrol users and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Each household member records a face and voice sample so the mirror can switch profiles; lighting and speaker levels are tuned.

buildSteps.title: Connect the home
buildSteps.detail: The mirror joins the local network, pairs with Matter/Thread or Zigbee devices, and scenes are set up.

buildSteps.title: Test privacy and update
buildSteps.detail: Camera shutter, data retention and firmware updates are verified before the device is trusted in a bathroom or bedroom.

prerequisites.tech: Half-silvered mirror glass and bright displays
prerequisites.why: without them the screen is invisible behind the reflection.
keeps biometric data local, which matters for a device used in private rooms.

prerequisites.tech: Far-field microphone arrays and wake-word detection
prerequisites.why: lets the mirror hear commands over running water and background noise.

prerequisites.tech: Small language models that run on edge hardware
prerequisites.why: full conversational assistants still lean on cloud servers, raising latency and privacy concerns.
Matter and Thread let one device control hardware from many manufacturers.

pathway.milestone: DIY builds and niche commercial mirrors with basic display, voice and smart-home control
pathway.unlocks: proof that the form factor is usable in a daily routine.

pathway.milestone: fitness and wellness mirrors with on-screen coaching and AI-generated feedback
pathway.unlocks: a paying use case that justifies the hardware cost.

pathway.milestone: on-device assistants that handle recognition and conversation without sending video or audio off the device
pathway.unlocks: acceptance in bathrooms and bedrooms where cameras are otherwise unwelcome.

pathway.milestone: ambient home interfaces that blend mirror, display and household control
pathway.unlocks: a screen that is useful whenever someone is in the room, rather than a device that must be picked up.
